## Tracking Clothing Patterns in Public Spaces

This report is based on clothing observations collected in public spaces. The data is gathered using a Google Form and is automatically updated through Google Sheets.

The dataset includes information on clothing type, style, and the number of upper-body layers worn. This report analyses these variables to explore common clothing habits and trends in public spaces.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Load data directly from Google Sheets (published as CSV)
data <- read_csv("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vQSUyvHX8BS8gfAqPamvdmuIpN4_9LRPwhzbsrVw9yfXvovTytSyY1Rp8sfX1ep_F_sQd26VsTQK2Y5/pub?output=csv")

data <- data %>%
  rename(
    clothing_type = contains("main type of clothing"),
    layers = contains("upper-body layers"),
    style = contains("describe")
  )

# Bar chart 1
data %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = clothing_type, fill = clothing_type)) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Clothing Types",
       x = "Clothing type",
       y = "Count")

# Bar chart 2
data %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = style, fill = style)) +
  labs(title = "Clothing Style Distribution",
       x = "Style",
       y = "Count")

# Summary
total_obs <- nrow(data)

most_common_type <- data %>%
  count(clothing_type) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  pull(clothing_type)

most_common_style <- data %>%
  count(style) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  pull(style)

mean_layers <- data %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(layers, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(mean)

max_layers <- max(data$layers, na.rm = TRUE)
```

This dataset contains `r total_obs` observations collected from public spaces.

The most commonly observed clothing type is `r most_common_type`, indicating it appears most frequently.

The most common clothing style is `r most_common_style`, showing a dominant style trend.

On average, people wear approximately `r round(mean_layers, 2)` upper-body layers.

The maximum number of upper-body layers observed is `r max_layers`.
